metas.name: Agriculture - Aracataca Cut Palms
metas.note: These palms where the crown has been cut, are very often found near Aracataca and some smaller towns North of it.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Agriculture - Banana
metas.note: In general, banana plantation can be found mostly in Quindio and Magdalena, sometimes in Northwest-Antioquia and Cordoba, and rarely in surrounding provinces of Quindio.
metas.footer: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Agriculture - Banana - Cloudy Gen 3
metas.note:
Large amounts of banana plants in plantations are commonly found in different areas.

Paired with Cloudy Gen 3 Coverage, they're most common in Northwestern Antioquia.
metas.footer: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Agriculture - Banana - Dry
metas.note: In Magdalena you will often see banana plantations in a dry sandy/dirty area with mountains to your east.
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Agriculture - Banana - Hedge
metas.note: In Quindio you will commonly find banana plantations behind hedges.
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Agriculture - Banana - Small Field / No Hedge
metas.note: In the states surrounding Quindio you will find smaller banana plantations along the road not behind hedges.
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Agriculture - Coffee
metas.note:
The coffee belt stretches in the valley between Medellin and Cali. In the North, you will only find it near the Venezuelan border.

Olives and Tea have a very similar distribution.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Agriculture - Common Guava
metas.note: Common Guava mostly appears in the valley between the western and the central mountain range in Colombia, but it can also appear in other valleys.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Agriculture - Guadua Bamboo
metas.note: Guadua Bamboo plantations are found mainly in Caldas, but also in the adjecent Tolima, Quindio and Risaralda.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Agriculture - Oil Palms
metas.note: Oilpalms can be found mainly in Meta and Casanare. They are also very common around the 45 near Fundacion and Aracataca. Sometimes, you can find them in Barrancabermeja.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane will mainly be found in Cauca and Valle de Cauca.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Architecture - Guatape
metas.note: Bright Colored Houses & Unique Pavement.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Architecture - Straw/Thatched Roofs
metas.note: Houses with roofs like this are commonly found along the coast, especially near Cartagena and Barranquilla.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Car Meta - Gen 3 - white/blue striped car
metas.note: Gen 3 with the white-blue car follows a straight line between Cartagena and Medellín, has partial coverage along Route 80 west of Bosconia, as well as along Route 45 north of Bucaramanga and east of Medellín.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Car Meta - Gen 4 - Grey Car
metas.note: Gen 4 coverage with the grey car is not found north of Montería, has a gap between Bucaramanga and Bogotá, forms a 'staircase' pattern with right angles at Medellín and Bogotá, covers areas around Bucaramanga, and has a missing section around Popayán.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Car Meta - Gen 4 - White Car
metas.note: Gen 4 with the white car has no coverage south of Cali, very little around Medellín, and forms a curved pattern around Medellín.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Car Meta - Leticia
metas.note:
This unique vehicle can be found in and around Leticia, the Southernmost town in Colombia.

NOTE: The long concrete blocks seen in the bottom left corner are a reliable way of recognising the road North of Leticia.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Car Meta - Providencia
metas.note: The island of Providencia, located roughly 90 kilometres North of San Andrés, is home to this unique grey truck.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Car Meta - San Andres
metas.note: Coverage on the Caribbean island of San Andrés was taken by this distinct white car.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Coverage Meta - "Gen 5" Glitch
metas.note: A camera glitch that makes a part of the image look very saturated can be found in southern Colombia.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Arauca Rift
metas.note: On the road in Arauca and in the city of Arauca in northeastern Colombia, there is virtually only cloudy, bad weather coverage. Furthermore, there was a small camera glitch where you can see this small rift northeast of the driving direction.
metas.footer: Source: Tipp des Tages on the German Discord Server

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Double Google Car
metas.note: A Second Google Car is visible in many random spots. The most prominent spots are the 26 in Cauca, Vda. Chontaduro (near Popoyan) and the road between Pital and Tarqui.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Double Google Car - Aguachica
metas.note: This instance of a second google car can be seen on Carrera 4, an offroad of the 45 near Aguachica.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Double Google Car - Villavicencio
metas.note: This instance of a second google car can be seen on the east-west road, directly south of Guayuriba River, which is south of Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Embalse Calima
metas.note: Large lake, mostly winter coverage. A small stretch also has summer coverage.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Foggy & Rainy Coverage
metas.note: If you see rainy coverage, combined with strong fog, you're on the 64.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Grey Car, 2023 copyright
metas.note: This combination can be found on the 65 in Caqueta and the 45 in Putumayo.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - La Florida
metas.note: Rainy coverage with very orange-brown soil can be found on this road to La Florida.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Rainy Coverage
metas.note: Rainy coverage is most common on the highways 20, 24, 50 and 64.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Sogamoso Lake
metas.note: If you see a lake, paired with an overexposed Gen 4 camera, you're probably on this lake south of Sogamoso.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Stick Meta
metas.note: This stick on the camera can be found between El Guio and El Boral (near the Cundinamarca-Meta border near Villavicencio)
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Arauca
metas.note: On this road, you can see a sunset through the clouds. It's not always easy to recognize, however.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Hato Corozal
metas.note: On this road, you can see a slight sunset through the clouds. It is pretty flat, with mountains in the Northwest.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Barichara Pavement
metas.note: This unique cobblestone pavement is found is the historic town of Barichara, Santander.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Barranquilla Roadbollard
metas.note: In Barranquilla, you can often find this bollard with roadnames on intersections.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Buenaventura Truck Spam Road
metas.note: The stretch of the 40 to Buenaventura is an important route for trucks, so if you see many trucks, it's worth a thought.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Caldas Polepaint
metas.note: orange & blue
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Cauca/Narino Polepaint
metas.note: Yellow with dark numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Coastal Antioquia Polepaint
metas.note: Green paint with yellow numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Electricity Counter - Oval
metas.note:
Usually pretty tall with oval windows, circle windows might not be as trustworthy.

Very common as there are few plastic counters in this region.
metas.footer: Source: The CoCo Document by Blinky

metas.name: Infrastructure - European Bollard
metas.note: This european-style (specifically spanish style bollard) is found in Cundinamarca, but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - H-shaped lamp attachment
metas.note: H-shaped lamp attachment plates can be found in Bogota.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Huila Polepaint
metas.note: Orange paint with black numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Ibague Lamp
metas.note:
This red lamp style is unique to Tolima province.

Note by MB: I only found it in Ibague, not in any other towns in Tolima. Also, the meta is more about the color and the shape of the lamp, not about the arrangement of the lights.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Megabus
metas.note: Green or yellow, modern bus. Often on a dedicated bus lane. Found in Pereira metropolitan area.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Pole Marking - Antioquia
metas.note: These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - QR-Code Sticker
metas.note: Found in Barranquilla and Santa Marta
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Rectangular lamp attachment
metas.note: Rectangular lamp attachment plates can be found mainly in Medellin, sometimes further North, especially in Monteria and Cucuta.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Risaralda/Choco Polepaint
metas.note: Yellow paint with red numbers. Found all over Risaralda and the towns of Istmina and Quibdo in Choco.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Sarawak Pole
metas.note: Asymmetrical poles with a "Sarawak" extension (a vertical stalk coming out the top), can often be found East of Andes. Note that this pole is not 100%, and has been spotted elsewhere.
metas.footer: Source: Meat of the Day on ScripterCord

metas.name: Infrastructure - Spikes
metas.note: These spikes can be found on the 40 and the 62.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Barranquilla
metas.note: The uniquely shaped supporting metal piece can be found in Barranquilla. (Similar to the Providencia design)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Providencia
metas.note: Providencia street lights are green and supported by a trapezoidal sheet of metal underneath. (The metal sheet without a green lamp can also be found in Barranquilla)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tinto Bus
metas.note: This red bus drives in the town (not the country) Armenia.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tolima Poletag
metas.note: Orange tag with white numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - TransLago vans
metas.note: TransLogo vans are common throughtout Boyaca Department. You will most often see them on the routes Tunja-Sogamoso and Tunja-Duitama.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Transmetro
metas.note: White Transmetro buses can be found in Barranquilla.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tumaco
metas.note: If you see many puddles and a pavement out of '+' shaped stones, you're in Tumaco.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Pole
metas.note: If you see these poletops you will find yourself in Valle Del Cauca.
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Polepaint
metas.note: Yellow, with black numbers. Several digits can be in one row.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Infrastructure - Villavicencio Bike Lane Road
metas.note: If you see a bike lane, and get East of Andes vibes, you're most likely on the road through Los Tobitos to Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Landscape - Deep grey & stony soil in Gen 3
metas.note: This type of soil can be found in towns near the pacific coast.
metas.footer: Source: Orion

metas.name: Landscape - East of Andes Landscape
metas.note:
East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.

Since it's to the east of the Andes, you may see mountains in the west, but never in the east.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Guatape Hill
metas.note: This striking cone-shaped mountain can often be seen from the surrounding area of Guatape.
metas.footer: Source: Tipp des Tages on the German Discord Server

metas.name: Landscape - Guaviare Orange Road
metas.note: The only road in Guaviare goes from to Guaviare (city), and continues south up until Vda. El Trueno. It can be recognized by the orange-looking dust on the road.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Landscape - La Guajira
metas.note: This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Northern Landscape
metas.note: The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Orocue Road
metas.note: This road leading from the 65 to the town of Orocue is characterized by its unique angle and the orange/brown dirt.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Landscape - Paramos
metas.note:
Paramos refers to alpine tundra ecosystems located in the mountains. These kinds of regions are easy to guess by how little vegetation grows here. The best clue is these odd looking pants. ( giant rosette plants ).

Note by MB: In my experience, this appears most commonly south of Bogota, still in the capital district.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Landscape - Pasto Hills
metas.note:
In southern Colombia, around the city of Pasto, there are hilly fields that are unique in that they are bordered by hedges. The hedges are very thick and form very distinctive lines on the hills. It almost gives off a “British” vibe. If you are sure that it is Colombia, this is a very good meta, but such fields with hedges also occur in Ecuador.

!! In very rare cases, such hedges on hills can also occur in other parts of Colombia. !!
metas.footer: Source: Tipp des Tages on the German Discord Server

metas.name: Landscape - Santa Rosalia
metas.note: Santa Rosalia is the only town covered in Vichada. So if you see red/orange dirt in an urban Gen 4 loc, you should go there.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Landscape - Swamp Road + Extremely Sunny
metas.note: If you see a swamp road with extremely sunny coverage, you're probably on the 74 in Sucre.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Landscape - Swamp Roads
metas.note: The 74, the 78 and a few other roads more north have very swampy parts, you can see on the map where these are by zooming.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Landscape - Unique Road - 78 west of Pailitas
metas.note: This road is characterised by low clouds and a towering mountain in the east.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Landscape - Unique Road - Ruta 90 Landbridge
metas.note:
You can recognise the narrow Ruta 90 landbridge between Barranquilla and Cienaga thanks to the dashed yellow lines and shallow bodies of water next to the road. Open ocean can often be seen to the north.

NOTE: In the older Generation 3 coverage, you will also see tall mountains in the distance.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Unique Road - Uribia to Puerto Boliviar
metas.note: You can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of La Guajira landscape (extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti), the straightness and the train track always present to the East.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Landscape - Vichada Red Dirt
metas.note: Vichada is characterize by hazy Gen 4 coverage and Red Dirt.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Misc - Afro-Colombians
metas.note: As a result of slave trade, the Pacific coast of Colombia is home to an overwhelming majority of Afro-Colombians.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt

metas.name: Trekker - Trebal Resort Trekker
metas.note: This trekker can be recognized by the unique pavement and houses.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Vegetation - Cacti
metas.note: Cacti are most commonly found in the North near Valledupar. Sometimes they can appear in Huila, too.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Vegetation - Colombian Mahogany
metas.note: This tree is found mainly around Medellin, but it has been spotted in other random spots.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Vegetation - Kapok Tree
metas.note: The Kapok tree can be found throughout Colombia, but is most common between the central and eastern mountain range.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Vegetation - Quindio Wax Palm
metas.note: This palm is found in mountainous regions of Colombia, mainly in Quindio, as the name suggests.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Vegetation - Veracruz Trees
metas.note: In Colombia you will most commonly find these trees that appear to have a knot on top of their trunk in the dark red areas. The province of Cordoba has the most gen 4 out of the others so if you see these in gen 4 consider Cordoba. (If the area is flat/semi hilly, You can find these trees in the mountains aswell everywhere)
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Vegetation - Wide Trees
metas.note: These wide trees, usually near fences, are found in Northern regions, especially near Monteria and Sincelejo.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo
